chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He was asked about fruit, when is its sale permissible? He said: 'If there is abundant fruit in one place, and some of it has been fed to the birds (or ripened), then the sale of all the fruit becomes permissible. If it is of one kind, its sale is not permissible until it is fed. If there are different kinds, nothing from it is sold until each kind is fed individually, then those kinds are sold.'

key_terms.أَطْعَمَ: Fed (referring to ripening or being eaten by birds)

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to sell fruit according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of Imam al-Sadiq, this hadith refines the fiqh of *bay' al-thimar* by distinguishing between localized abundance and distinct varieties, requiring the 'eating' (*it'am*) stage to ensure quality and prevent *gharar* (uncertainty). This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical certainty in trade, ensuring that the commodity is not only present but also viable for consumption before financial exchange.
